## Description
Dynamic Albedo of Neutrons (DAN): This instrument, carried by the Curiosity rover,&#10;&#9;&#9; uses a pulsing neutron generator to detect hydrogen in the shallow subsurface &#10;&#9;&#9; (up to ~50 cm depth).  It identifies water-bearing minerals or ice with high sensitivity &#10;&#9;&#9; (detecting as low as 0.1% water content). Hydrated minerals are the only hydrogen-bearing &#10;&#9;&#9; compounds found in significant quantity on Mars.&#10;&#9;&#9; &#10;&#9;&#9; Neutron moderation by hydrogen :&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;- The PNG fires a short pulse (~1–2 µs, up to 10 Hz) of 14.1 MeV fast neutrons into the &#10;&#9;&#9;  ground from ~80 cm above the surface. &#10;&#9;&#9;- Neutrons penetrate ~0.5–1 m into the regolith, colliding with atomic nuclei along the way.&#10;&#9;&#9;- A neutron that hits a hydrogen nucleus (nearly the same mass as the neutron, like two &#10;&#9;&#9;  billiard balls) loses roughly half its energy in a single collision.  &#10;&#9;&#9;- Other nuclei (oxygen, silicon, iron, etc.) are much heavier and barely slow the neutron.&#10;&#9;&#9;- The moderated neutrons that escape back up to the surface are detected by two ³He &#10;&#9;&#9;  proportional counters in the DE module, which record both the energy (thermal vs. epithermal) &#10;&#9;&#9;  and the time-of-flight after each pulse.&#10;&#9;&#9;  &#10;&#9;&#9;  https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/mars-rover-carries-device-for-underground-scouting/&#10;&#9;&#9;
